A request starts work rather than proves execution.

questions.prompt: What is a better asset-data quality measure than row count alone?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training case — not a field record.

Controller asset A-104 serial OLD7 is replaced by serial NEW9 using the same hostname and IP address. CMMS still attaches work orders to OLD7; DCIM lists the rack relationship; BMS discovery overwrites the serial but loses the old maintenance history. A retired rack still draws power, although its 5 kW reservation has already been released. An audit checks five convenient records from a population of 400.
options: The largest possible number of duplicate entries
Only the percentage of records containing a display name
The number of unreviewed discovery imports
Accuracy/completeness of required identities and relationships with timely updates
explanations: Duplicates can obscure the actual population.
A populated name field does not establish identity or relationship accuracy.
Import volume does not prove accepted data quality.
Rows can be numerous yet wrong or stale.

questions.prompt: What can the five-record convenience audit establish?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training case — not a field record.

Controller asset A-104 serial OLD7 is replaced by serial NEW9 using the same hostname and IP address. CMMS still attaches work orders to OLD7; DCIM lists the rack relationship; BMS discovery overwrites the serial but loses the old maintenance history. A retired rack still draws power, although its 5 kW reservation has already been released. An audit checks five convenient records from a population of 400.
options: A precise population defect rate without assumptions
That no further corrective action can be needed
Findings for the selected records with stated sampling limits
Verified accuracy of all 400 assets
explanations: Convenience sampling lacks a justified statistical basis here.
Observed issues and untested records remain relevant.
It cannot prove the entire population is correct.
The sample and selection do not support that universal claim.

questions.prompt: How should a conflict between discovery and controlled field evidence be handled?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training case — not a field record.

Controller asset A-104 serial OLD7 is replaced by serial NEW9 using the same hostname and IP address. CMMS still attaches work orders to OLD7; DCIM lists the rack relationship; BMS discovery overwrites the serial but loses the old maintenance history. A retired rack still draws power, although its 5 kW reservation has already been released. An audit checks five convenient records from a population of 400.
options: Create two active assets with the same identity and no explanation
Preserve both observations, assess provenance and resolve through the assigned owner
Always favor the newest timestamp regardless of source
Always discard discovery because automation cannot help
explanations: That preserves ambiguity rather than resolves it.
Automatic overwrite can destroy useful evidence.
Recency alone does not establish correctness.
Discovery can provide valuable observations within its limits.

questions.prompt: What closes an asset-governance corrective action?
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training case — not a field record.

Controller asset A-104 serial OLD7 is replaced by serial NEW9 using the same hostname and IP address. CMMS still attaches work orders to OLD7; DCIM lists the rack relationship; BMS discovery overwrites the serial but loses the old maintenance history. A retired rack still draws power, although its 5 kW reservation has already been released. An audit checks five convenient records from a population of 400.
options: Evidence of the required correction and its effectiveness against the finding
Only assigning the action to someone
Only changing its status to green
Only repeating the original audit wording
explanations: An updated record alone may not prove the process weakness is resolved.
Ownership begins the response.
A label does not demonstrate the result.
Restating the finding does not correct it.
